                   INTRODUCTION TO CLASSROOM MANAGEMENT

Topic- 001:

Classroom management is a very important part of the professional development of teachers. A
teachers’ duty is not only to teach the class but also to handle the management issues in classroom
for effective teaching and learning process.

In this lecture, the following topics of classroom management are discussed:

   -   Elements of classroom management
   -   Classroom management approaches and strategies
   -   Models of classroom management
   -   Teacher’s role in classroom management
   -   Classroom management and the curriculum
   -   Discipline
   -   Bullying and social-emotional learning

Topic – 002: Definition of Classroom Management:

Classroom management embodies:

   -   Effective teaching of content (classroom management problems arise because a teacher is
       sometimes not sure of what she is teaching)
   -   Powerful teaching strategies (It is extremely important to use effective teaching strategies so
       that less classroom management problems arise. Sometimes, the problems in classroom arise
       because teachers do not know the teaching strategies)
   -   An organizational structure to support productive learning (the seating arrangement of
       classroom, are students sitting in rows or groups?)
   -   Effective use of social-emotional domains of learning
   -   The most successful teachers approach management as a process of establishing and
       maintaining effective learning environments

Q. Strategies to Maintain Discipline
Educators use various techniques to create a positive and orderly classroom
environment. These strategies may include setting clear rules, reinforcing positive
behavior, using non-verbal cues, and involving students in rule-setting.
Q. Teaching with Limited Resources & Motivating Student
When faced with resource constraints, teachers can maximize available materials,
build rapport with students, and engage in creative activities. Motivating students
involves understanding their interests, providing relevant content, and fostering a
supportive learning atmosphere.

Q. Systematic Procedure for Record Keeping
Effective record keeping involves identifying transactions, recording them in a
journal, classifying their nature, posting to a ledger, balancing accounts, and
preparing financial statements. It ensures accurate financial tracking and compliance
with legal requirements.
Q. Establishing Caring Connections
Teachers build positive relationships with students by conducting surveys,
practicing open communication, and getting to know students outside the classroom.
Creating a caring environment fosters trust and enhances student engagement.
Q. Teachers Attributes in Teaching Social Skills
Effective teachers exhibit qualities such as empathy, adaptability, patience, and
lifelong learning. They model positive behavior, actively listen, and create a
supportive classroom culture.
Q. Incentives in the Classroom
Incentives, such as rewards or recognition, motivate students to participate and
excel. Teachers can use these incentives to reinforce desired behaviors and
encourage active engagement.
Q. Practice for Model for Rewards
Implementing a rewards system involves defining clear criteria for earning rewards,
consistently applying them, and ensuring they align with desired outcomes. It
encourages positive behavior and effort.
Q. Effective Behavioural Support Systems
These systems provide targeted interventions for students with behavioral
challenges. They involve collaboration among teachers, counselors, and parents to
address individual needs.

Q. School Discipline
School discipline encompasses rules, consequences, and procedures to maintain
order and promote a safe learning environment. It includes both preventive measures
and corrective actions.
Q. School-wide Preventive Discipline Practices
These practices involve creating a positive school culture, emphasizing prevention
over punishment, and promoting respectful behavior throughout the entire school
community.
Q. Classroom Discipline
Within the classroom, teachers manage behavior, enforce rules, and address
disruptions. Effective classroom discipline ensures a conducive learning
environment.
Q. Specific Discipline Programmes
Some schools implement specialized programs to address specific behavioral issues,
such as anti-bullying programs or conflict resolution initiatives.
Q. Bullying
Bullying refers to repeated aggressive behavior intended to harm or intimidate
others. Schools work to prevent and address bullying through awareness campaigns,
policies, and support systems
Q. Bullying Preventive Programmes
These programs aim to reduce bullying incidents by promoting awareness, teaching
empathy, and fostering a positive school climate. They involve strategies such as
peer mediation, conflict resolution, and anti-bullying campaigns.
Q. Social Intervention Strategies to Control Bullying
Educators implement social interventions to address bullying behavior. These
strategies may include group discussions, role-playing, and teaching assertiveness
skills to prevent and manage bullying.

Q. Parent-Teacher Partnerships & CM
Collaborative efforts between parents and teachers enhance classroom management.
Effective communication, involvement in school activities, and shared expectations
contribute to a positive learning environment.
Q. Violence & Classroom Management
Managing violence involves setting clear rules, addressing disruptive behavior
promptly, and providing alternatives to aggression. Teachers use de-escalation
techniques and conflict resolution to maintain safety.

Q. Strategies to Maintain Discipline
Educators use various techniques to create a positive and orderly classroom
environment. These strategies may include setting clear rules, reinforcing positive
behavior, using non-verbal cues, and involving students in rule-setting.
Q. Teaching with Limited Resources & Motivating Student
When faced with resource constraints, teachers can maximize available materials,
build rapport with students, and engage in creative activities. Motivating students
involves understanding their interests, providing relevant content, and fostering a
supportive learning atmosphere.

Q. Systematic Procedure for Record Keeping
Effective record keeping involves identifying transactions, recording them in a
journal, classifying their nature, posting to a ledger, balancing accounts, and
preparing financial statements. It ensures accurate financial tracking and compliance
with legal requirements.
Q. Establishing Caring Connections
Teachers build positive relationships with students by conducting surveys,
practicing open communication, and getting to know students outside the classroom.
Creating a caring environment fosters trust and enhances student engagement.
Q. Teachers Attributes in Teaching Social Skills
Effective teachers exhibit qualities such as empathy, adaptability, patience, and
lifelong learning. They model positive behavior, actively listen, and create a
supportive classroom culture.
Q. Incentives in the Classroom
Incentives, such as rewards or recognition, motivate students to participate and
excel. Teachers can use these incentives to reinforce desired behaviors and
encourage active engagement.
Q. Practice for Model for Rewards
Implementing a rewards system involves defining clear criteria for earning rewards,
consistently applying them, and ensuring they align with desired outcomes. It
encourages positive behavior and effort.
Q. Effective Behavioural Support Systems
These systems provide targeted interventions for students with behavioral
challenges. They involve collaboration among teachers, counselors, and parents to
address individual needs.

Q. School Discipline
School discipline encompasses rules, consequences, and procedures to maintain
order and promote a safe learning environment. It includes both preventive measures
and corrective actions.
Q. School-wide Preventive Discipline Practices
These practices involve creating a positive school culture, emphasizing prevention
over punishment, and promoting respectful behavior throughout the entire school
community.
Q. Classroom Discipline
Within the classroom, teachers manage behavior, enforce rules, and address
disruptions. Effective classroom discipline ensures a conducive learning
environment.
Q. Specific Discipline Programmes
Some schools implement specialized programs to address specific behavioral issues,
such as anti-bullying programs or conflict resolution initiatives.
Q. Bullying
Bullying refers to repeated aggressive behavior intended to harm or intimidate
others. Schools work to prevent and address bullying through awareness campaigns,
policies, and support systems
Q. Bullying Preventive Programmes
These programs aim to reduce bullying incidents by promoting awareness, teaching
empathy, and fostering a positive school climate. They involve strategies such as
peer mediation, conflict resolution, and anti-bullying campaigns.
Q. Social Intervention Strategies to Control Bullying
Educators implement social interventions to address bullying behavior. These
strategies may include group discussions, role-playing, and teaching assertiveness
skills to prevent and manage bullying.

Q. Parent-Teacher Partnerships & CM
Collaborative efforts between parents and teachers enhance classroom management.
Effective communication, involvement in school activities, and shared expectations
contribute to a positive learning environment.
Q. Violence & Classroom Management
Managing violence involves setting clear rules, addressing disruptive behavior
promptly, and providing alternatives to aggression. Teachers use de-escalation
techniques and conflict resolution to maintain safety.

1. How do parent-teacher partnerships affect classroom learning?

Parent-teacher partnerships foster collaboration between home and school, which improves
student learning. When parents and teachers communicate effectively, they can support the
child’s educational goals, monitor progress, and address challenges early. This partnership helps
create a consistent learning environment, increases student motivation, and improves behavior
and academic achievement.

2. Why should we avoid the "nice teacher syndrome"?

The "nice teacher syndrome" refers to teachers trying too hard to be liked by students, often at
the cost of enforcing rules. Avoiding this is important because it can lead to a lack of classroom
discipline, students taking advantage of the teacher, and reduced respect for authority. Teachers
should maintain a balance of warmth and firmness to manage classrooms effectively.

3. How does overall school discipline management relate to social competence?

School discipline management directly influences the development of social competence. A
well-disciplined environment encourages students to follow rules, respect others, manage
conflicts peacefully, and engage in prosocial behaviors. Students learn to regulate emotions,
cooperate with peers, and develop a sense of responsibility, all of which are key components of
social competence.

4. What are penalties? Give four classroom examples.

Penalties are consequences assigned for violating rules or exhibiting undesirable behavior to
discourage recurrence. Examples include:

      Loss of recess or free time.
      Extra assignments or written apologies.
      Temporary removal from a group activity.
      Detention or staying back after class.

5. What is a systemic behavior record?

A systemic behavior record is a structured method for documenting and tracking students'
behavior over time. It helps teachers:

      Identify behavioral patterns.
      Monitor improvements or regressions.
      Communicate behavior issues with parents or school counselors.
      Develop targeted interventions for students with repeated infractions.

6. Why is teacher training important in classroom discipline?

Teacher training equips educators with strategies to manage student behavior effectively. It
improves their skills in conflict resolution, communication, classroom organization, and
understanding child psychology. Trained teachers can prevent and handle disruptions, apply
appropriate discipline methods, and create a productive learning environment.

7. What are some social problems of aggressive students?

Aggressive students may:

      Struggle to maintain friendships.
      Engage in bullying or violent behavior.
      Face academic failure due to suspensions or distractions.
      Be rejected by peers and isolated.
      Develop low self-esteem or behavioral disorders if not addressed.

      Model respectful and empathetic behavior.
      Teach conflict resolution skills.
      Organize role-play and social skill activities.
      Reinforce positive social interactions through rewards and praise.

                                    Glossary

 Adherence
Adherence mean to act, action, or quality of adhering. the obeying of a rule or law
 Behaviour Modification
Behaviour modification attempts to promote desirable behaviour and eliminate undesirable
behaviour. It attempts to bring changes in student behaviour through the use of different strategies.
 BULLYING
Bullying occurs when a person willfully and repeatedly exercises power over another with hostile
or malicious intent.
 Cookbook Management
This is an eclectic approach that may consist of applying a prescription of ‘do’s and don’ts’,
without any obviously consistent rationale. It may consist of adaptation of a number of most
effective approaches which suit the situation or group of individuals.
 Covert Management Approaches
Covert Management Approaches are those approaches which have an implied existence. They are
not explicitly stated by teachers but are expected behaviours advocated through a school wide
adherence to core values and norms.
 Curriculum
Curriculum basically is a plan of action for the entire school. The curriculum consists of the
ongoing experiences of children under the guidance of the school. It represents a special
environment for helping children achieve self realization through active participation within the
school.
 Expectations
Expectations are the norms applied to a specific situation.
 Extrinsic Motivation

Maha Malik’s Compilation

Extrinsic motivation occurs when a student is driven to perform behaviour in order to win a reward
or avoid a punishment.
 Intimidation
Intimidation is an approach used by teachers to control student behaviour. This is an overt approach
in which the teacher uses power to regulate student behaviour. Most of the practices under
intimidation are negative.
 Intrinsic Motivation
Intrinsic motivation is a desire to attain targets for the sake of learning.
 Negative Consequences
Negative consequences are the penalties that students face when they bypass or disobey rules.
 Norms
Norms are unwritten rules stating what students should and should not do. They regulate and
control behavior.
 Overlapping
Overlapping means handling two or more situations or activities simultaneously. A teacher who
can instruct a group of students while responding to student concerns from outside of the group
can keep an entire classroom working smoothly.
 Overt Management Approaches
Overt Management approaches are those approaches in which teachers use an explicit effort to
manage classroom based behavioural and management issues.
 School Culture
School culture is a set of unstated expectations and assumptions that direct the activities of school
personnel and students.
 Student Team Learning
Student Team Learning is a cooperative learning structure and is an instructional rather than a
disciplinary strategy.

                   INTRODUCTION TO CLASSROOM MANAGEMENT

Topic- 001:

Classroom management is a very important part of the professional development of teachers. A
teachers’ duty is not only to teach the class but also to handle the management issues in
classroom for effective teaching and learning process.

In this lecture, the following topics of classroom management are discussed:

   -   Elements of classroom management
   -   Classroom management approaches and strategies
   -   Models of classroom management
   -   Teacher’s role in classroom management
   -   Classroom management and the curriculum
   -   Discipline
   -   Bullying and social-emotional learning

Topic – 002: Definition of Classroom Management:

Classroom management embodies:

   -   Effective teaching of content (classroom management problems arise because a teacher is
       sometimes not sure of what she is teaching)
   -   Powerful teaching strategies (It is extremely important to use effective teaching strategies
       so that less classroom management problems arise. Sometimes, the problems in
       classroom arise because teachers do not know the teaching strategies)
   -   An organizational structure to support productive learning (the seating arrangement of
       classroom, are students sitting in rows or groups?)
   -   Effective use of social-emotional domains of learning
   -   The most successful teachers approach management as a process of establishing and
       maintaining effective learning environments

EDU305
1. Introduction to Classroom Management

Classroom management refers to the strategies, techniques, and methods that teachers use to
maintain a positive and productive learning environment. Effective classroom management
ensures that students are engaged, respectful, and focused on learning, while minimizing
disruptive behavior. It involves organizing the classroom, setting clear expectations, and
fostering an atmosphere conducive to learning.

Key aspects include:

   •   Setting expectations: Establishing rules for behavior.
   •   Promoting engagement: Keeping students focused and involved in lessons.
   •   Preventing disruptions: Addressing and managing misbehavior when it occurs.

2. Classroom Control

Classroom control refers to a teacher's ability to manage student behavior in a way that ensures
the classroom environment remains orderly and conducive to learning. It includes maintaining
authority, responding to misbehavior appropriately, and using proactive strategies to prevent
disruptions. Classroom control can be achieved through:

   •   Clear, consistent rules.
   •   Positive reinforcement of good behavior.
   •   Use of authority and discipline when necessary.

3. Physical Seating & Classroom Management

The physical seating arrangement plays a crucial role in classroom management as it directly
affects student interaction, focus, and participation. By strategically placing students, teachers
can:

   •   Minimize distractions.
   •   Encourage collaboration or individual work, depending on the task.
   •   Ensure that all students can see the board, access learning materials, and are not overly
       distracted by others.

Common seating arrangements include:

   •   Rows for individual work or exams.

   •   Circles or clusters for group discussions or collaborative activities.
   •   U-shaped for class discussions, allowing the teacher to move freely among students.

4. Overt Management Approaches

Overt management approaches are those that involve visible, direct actions by the teacher to
maintain control and structure in the classroom. These strategies are typically explicit and
observable by students and may include:

   •   Giving direct instructions.
   •   Setting and enforcing rules.
   •   Using non-verbal cues (e.g., eye contact, hand gestures) to maintain focus.
   •   Providing positive or corrective feedback.

These approaches aim to manage student behavior by making expectations clear and ensuring
that students understand the consequences of their actions.

5. Overt & Covert Management Approaches

Overt management approaches are visible strategies where the teacher directly intervenes in
classroom behavior (e.g., raising voice, giving instructions). In contrast, covert management
approaches are more subtle and indirect. They involve influencing students' behavior without
overt intervention. Covert approaches can include:

   •   Setting up the classroom environment to prevent disruptions.
   •   Using quiet signals or cues for students to refocus.
   •   Establishing routines that students follow without the teacher needing to remind them
       constantly.

The combination of both overt and covert approaches allows teachers to balance direct control
with a more passive, self-regulating classroom environment.

6. Role of Teacher in Managing the Classroom

The role of the teacher in managing the classroom is multi-faceted:

   •   Leader: Providing clear guidance, establishing expectations, and modeling appropriate
       behavior.
   •   Facilitator: Creating an environment where students can learn and interact productively.
   •   Mediator: Resolving conflicts and addressing disruptive behavior in a fair and consistent
       manner.
   •   Motivator: Encouraging students to stay engaged and motivated, using praise and
       positive reinforcement.
   •   Observer: Monitoring student behavior and interactions to identify potential issues early
       on.

A teacher's role is crucial for maintaining an environment where students can thrive
academically and socially.

7. Effective Management

Effective management involves using appropriate strategies to create an environment where
learning can occur with minimal disruption. Effective management includes:

   •   Establishing clear expectations for behavior and learning.
   •   Building positive teacher-student relationships.
   •   Using consistent strategies to deal with misbehavior.
   •   Engaging students actively in the learning process.
   •   Adjusting management techniques based on student needs and behavior.

An effective classroom manager is proactive, flexible, and fair, ensuring that students feel safe,
respected, and motivated.

8. Models of Classroom Management

There are several models of classroom management that teachers can adopt, depending on their
teaching style, classroom environment, and student needs:

   •   The Assertive Discipline Model: Emphasizes clear rules and consistent enforcement of
       consequences.
   •   The Positive Behavior Support (PBS) Model: Focuses on rewarding positive behaviors
       to encourage a supportive classroom atmosphere.
   •   The Cooperative Discipline Model: Focuses on building student responsibility and
       engaging students in solving problems.
   •   The Classroom Organization and Management Model (COM): Emphasizes
       structuring the classroom to facilitate student engagement and minimize disruptions.

Each model provides a different approach to managing behavior, but all stress the importance of
clear expectations, positive reinforcement, and consistency.

9. Plan to Implement the Models with Students

To implement a classroom management model effectively, teachers must:

   1. Understand the model: Familiarize themselves with the chosen management model and
      its principles.
   2. Set clear rules and expectations: Clearly communicate these to students at the start of
      the year or term.

Being a teacher how will you handle problems of a student’s faced in school?

   1) Take Interest in Students’ Lives

in schools to address acute behavioral problems.

with each other.

help students learn how to interact respectfully, share ideas, and work in teams. These
experiences build communication skills, empathy, and cooperation, which are essential for
social development.

Unlike other approaches, it is considered a negative approach. Due to this reason, it is the
extreme opposite of intimidation. Here the teacher promotes maximum student freedom in
order to foster natural development of each individual’s full potential.

In intimidation the teacher is in threatening mode. And maintains disciplines by fearing and
threatening students. But in permissiveness teacher is in very loose control in the classroom.
His/her objective is to deliver lecture to the class and the teacher is not concerned about having
discipline in the class. So, this can be very dangerous as per as teaching and learning
conditioned are concerned.

In permissiveness teachers thinks that his/her sole purpose in is to deliver lecture and complete
teaching targets and if there is any behavioral issue in the classroom, he/she is totally ignoring
the issue.

   ▪   The teacher can lose authority in the class and can be considered a powerless figure. The

In the laissez-faire approach, the teacher exercises minimal control, does limited planning, and
allows students considerable freedom. The teacher focuses mainly on content delivery and pays
less attention to classroom discipline and management.

2. Strategies to identify needs of problem students

      Maintain student profiles and behavior portfolios.
      Observe students carefully in class.
      Monitor peer interactions.
      Coordinate with parents and counselors.
      Seek support from administrators and staff.

3. Rules for maintaining classroom discipline

      Establish rules at the beginning of the year.
      Develop rules with students.
      Reinforce rules regularly.
      Apply rules fairly and consistently.
      Define consequences for non-compliance.

4. Being a teacher, how do we monitor student work?

Teachers monitor learning through formal assessments, informal assessments, project work,
continuous observation, feedback, and assessment portfolios.

5. How students can self-regulate behavior and play an active role in classroom
management

Students can self-regulate by controlling emotions, reflecting on their behavior, solving problems
responsibly, participating in group activities, and following classroom rules.

6. Why should teachers prepare differentiated tasks?

Differentiated tasks accommodate learner differences, ensure participation of all students, reduce
frustration, and improve learning outcomes.

7. Importance of classroom rules

Classroom rules create discipline, establish boundaries, guide behavior, and support effective
teaching and learning.

8. Why do teachers make students’ seating fixed and use name cards?

Fixed seating and name cards help teachers identify students, maintain order, monitor behavior,

9. How can teachers control aggressiveness of unmet students?

Teachers should identify causes of aggression, provide counseling support, maintain caring
relationships, teach self-control, and involve parents when necessary.

10. Being a teacher, how to manage/control a classroom?

      Establish rules and routines.
      Create a positive climate.
      Monitor learning continuously.
      Organize seating and materials.
      Reinforce positive behavior.

11. Why is professional development important for teachers?

Professional development improves teachers’ classroom management, discipline handling, rule
setting, organization, and behavior management skills.

12. Importance of communication skills

Communication skills help teachers explain concepts clearly, build positive relationships, resolve
conflicts, and promote effective learning.

13. Effective learning

Effective learning occurs when content knowledge, pedagogy, classroom management, and
social-emotional learning work together in a positive environment.

14. How can a teacher manage student talk?

Teachers should establish communication rules, encourage turn-taking, use hand-raising
procedures, and ensure respectful discussions.

15. How would you engage students in class?

Use varied teaching methods, group work, cooperative learning, discussions, projects, and
meaningful tasks based on students’ interests.

16. How to work with negative reinforcement?

Long Questions
1. How should teachers maintain good behavior of students in class?

Teachers should establish rules at the beginning of the year, develop rules collaboratively with
students, reinforce expectations regularly, apply rules consistently, monitor behavior
continuously, and provide positive reinforcement. Building respectful relationships and
promoting self-control also help maintain discipline.

2. Why is it important to plan variety tasks?

Variety tasks reduce boredom, maintain interest, accommodate different learning styles,
encourage participation, and improve classroom discipline. Students become more engaged when
activities vary in format and interaction patterns.

3. Effective Teaching Skills

Effective teaching skills include:

      Strong content knowledge
      Pedagogical competence
      Classroom management skills
      Communication skills
      Monitoring and assessment abilities
      Ability to motivate students
      Social-emotional understanding

4. Stakeholders’ Role

Stakeholders include students, teachers, parents, administrators, principals, and the community.
They help maintain discipline, identify problems, follow school policies, build rapport, and
support effective learning environments.

5. Dimensions of Classroom Organization

The main dimensions are:

      Seating arrangements
      Teacher position

Behaviours that need modification:
   -   Fear and anxiety of various aspects of school life
   -   Gross misbehavior in class
   -   Substance abuse
   -   Learning difficulties e.g. dyslexia, autism, attention, deficit
   -   Criminal and delinquent activity

 Q. Covert management approaches usage
   -   School Assembly
   -   Tutorials
   -   Lesson Plans
   -   Sport Activities
   -   Extra Curricular Activities
   -   Behavioural interactions
   -   Out of school interaction

 Q. Physical seatings of classroom
While doing seating arrangement of students, there are many choices;
   -   Group seating in classroom
   -   Individual seating in classroom
   -   Pair seating
   -   Seating on a carpet etc.

 Q. Counseling services in school
   Professional support is required to deal with:

       a) Aggressive behavior
       b) Bullyism
       c) Criminal behavior
       d) Sadistic behavior
       e) extreme shyness

      f) lack of self-efficacy

 Q. Classroom control
Classroom control is a very important element of classroom management. Without
classroom control, there can be no classroom management. Teachers are the
biggest sources to maintain class control.
Teachers need to be:
   - Authoritative: students must feel the presence of the teacher. Teacher must
     be in full control, which is what called being authoritative in the class.
   - In command: A teacher must know how to follow her lesson plan. How
     students must behave during lesson. How the activities in classroom will be
     possible? Mastery on the content, pedagogy and management made the
     teacher in command.
   - Organized: It is extremely important for the teacher to be organized in the
     classroom.

Students need to:
   - Act responsibly: Hidden curriculum teaches the students how to behave in
     the classroom. What rules he should follow without asking? So,
     responsibility comes from following the hidden curriculum that is
     manifested through the behaviour patterns of the different stakeholders in
     the school.
   - Follow rules: Students need to follow rules which are mutually constructed
     by the students and teachers. Once they are mutually constructed then they
     need to be followed. So that an effective classroom control is possible.
   - Respect teachers: Students need to respect their teachers that come from the
     hidden curriculum. Without respecting the teacher in the classroom there can
     be no classroom control.
   - Take care of peers

 Q. Routine maintenance
Routine maintenance is carried out periodically-monthly, quarterly or even
annually depending on the agreed schedule by the class/school manager.

 Q. Self-Evaluation
Student behavioral self-evaluation

   1. Students should be encouraged to do their behavioral self-evaluation
   2. The behavioral records should have a section on self evaluation and students should fill
       that section themselves
   3. This exercise makes students more reflective and enables them to analysis their own
       behaviors

 Q. Kinds of outdoor activities
Outdoor activities are dependent on the age level of the students. These are also
dependent on the subjects they are dealt with. Outdoor activities are:

    Field trips
       These can be content related. They can deal with different subject areas. It can
       also be a recreation
    Nature experiments
       These are related with the science subjects.
    Research based studies of various phenomena
       These can be determined by the teachers.
    Fun activities, camping
       With academics other activities are also important for the students like
       camping. It includes both recreation and learning.
 Q. Practice with it-ness
Helpful hints:
    Stand where you can see all students when you present a lesson.
    Make eye contact with as many students as possible.
    Keep your face towards the students when you move towards the
     chalkboard.

   Stand at an angle to write on the chalkboard so that you an see as many
     students as possible.
   Circulate to various parts of room.
 Q. Communication skill
Communication can be verbal and non-verbal and just as in everyday life, poor
communication can cause unnecessary problems. Good communication skills and
being a good listener , as well as a good speaker , can help in preventing problems
in the classroom. When students feel that they are welcomed into a nonthreatening
environment where learning is encouraged, they usually come ready, willing, and
able to learn.
 Q. Overlapping
Overlapping means handling two or more situations or activities simultaneously.
A teacher who can instruct a group of students while responding to student
concerns from outside of the group can keep an entire classroom working
smoothly.
Practicing overlapping
Make eye contact with, move closer to, or stand beside a misbehaving student to
deter off task behavior while continuing to direct other activities.
Direct a question to a student who has not been paying attention to regain his/her
attention.
Remove an object a student is playing with without interrupting a presentation.
 Q. What is school culture?
School culture is a set of unstated expectations and assumptions that direct the
activities of school personnel and students.
It becomes the guide for behavior that is shared among members of the school at
large.
Culture is the stream of norms, values, beliefs, traditions and rituals built up over
time.
They must be upheld and communicated to the students as a way to prevent
behavioral issues in schools.

 Q. Story maps
A story map guides students to attend to the relevant parts of a story. It also helps
in giving a direction to the way a story is developed.

In planning the :

    Content
    Sequence of activities
    Material
    Room management
